Summary
Jack writes to Folke Roth about receiving Christmas packages, including canned fruit and other items, which arrived in good condition. He mentions that the packages had been in New Guinea for some time and were sent to the Australian mainland. Jack also discusses sending letters of thanks for received items and mentions Abe, who has been letterless for a while. Jack provides five negatives from the Headquarters of the 6th Army for Folke to develop and add to his collection. The letter concludes with Jack's health and well-being and his intention to write again upon receiving Folke's letter.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_13a) --- Dear Folke Roth: Haven't received my customary weekly letter from you which I imagine will come in tomorrow. Have some good news in that our Christmas packages finally arrived — most of them were terribly beaten up and almost all edible, even fit for table. However, it seems I was an exception. Your lot of canned fruit arrived intact and in perfect condition. The wrapping which the firm supplied in boxing, I think did the trick. I was rather surprised to open the box and find everything in its original attractive state. It was a real treat and something unheard of in Australia — especially since the war. The civilian girls in the office really went for it — and all went in nothing at all. Everybody has been getting packages and your office almost looked like a dep't store. And say — the garbage can got a good share of the booty. It seems that the packages laid around in New Guinea for some time, so they could be got to send them down to the Australian mainland. Cindy got a few other packages — a fruit cake from the Mothers Club. (which miraculously was in excellent condition — and a box containing some bottled delicacies from the Girls Club. Our army --- Page 2 (Beckerman_13b) --- acknowledge these with letters of thanks. Also received a box from Leah. You should ask her what was in it. There last few weeks have been almost letterless. Heard from Abe again and he appears to be O.K. Am going to answer him this evening. How are all of you getting along. Have you been getting any more pictures from Abe? How is my collection coming along? Here are some more to add. There are five negatives that I wish you'd develop and put into the collection. We took them at the Headquarters of the 6th Army. They are of the Chapel, outdoor theater, the hut we stayed in, and me of General Creager's house. Notice all the palm trees. This whole area was laid right out on the beach. Please keep all the negatives too. Everything here still going fine and health is still the best. We write again as soon as I receive your letter. Love and regards, Jack
